_comment: Model-tier matrix for review and dispatch calls. One row per task category. Each tier is an ordered list of {model, effort}. The first entry of a tier is the default. Later entries are used only when an earlier entry has no quota left, or when a provider's surplus lets a call lean one rung up on that same provider. Model names: 'bmo:...' and 'local:...' run on local GPUs and never use a paid account; 'opencode-go/...' and 'openai/...' run on those subscriptions; a bare name (sonnet, opus, fable) runs on the Claude subscription. Prices and benchmark scores come from the dated sources in each row's 'source' field.

coding.source: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index v1.5 (retrieved 2026-10-07); prices from the 2026-10-08 fetch-models snapshot (models.dev)
coding.note: Index scores: sonnet 5.5 = 68 (the leader), opus 5.5 = 66 (97%), fable 5.1 = 62 (91%), glm-5.3 = 54 (79%). Value (score percent divided by blended input/output price, models.dev, 2026-10-08): glm-5.3 27.4 pts/$ at $1.40/$4.40; deepseek-v4-pro $0.66/$1.98 (70.8 pts/$, scored for CAD, not coding); kimi-k2.7-code $0.95/$4 with no exact score; sonnet 16.7 pts/$ at $2/$10; opus 5.5 8.1 pts/$ at $4/$20; fable 3.2 pts/$ at $10/$50. So the default rung is a high-value opencode-go model at high effort, and the expensive Claude models are the last entries, not the first. bmo stays tier0: the AA score used for it belongs to a different artifact, and bmo's real served model is unverified, so treat this placement as unverified until something benchmarks the served model directly. kimi-k2.7-code, deepseek-v4-pro, qwen3.8-max and kimi-k3 have no exact coding score; they are picked for price and provider spread, not for a measured coding result.

general.source: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (no cached scores on 2026-10-08); prices from the 2026-10-08 fetch-models snapshot (models.dev)
general.note: No exact-model Intelligence Index score is cached for any model here (the last fetch found none), so this row copies coding's order: the default rung is the highest-value paid option at high effort, and the expensive Claude models come last. bmo stays tier0. The AA number used earlier for bmo belongs to a different artifact, and bmo's real served model is unverified, so treat this placement as unverified until something benchmarks the served model directly.

frontend-ui.source: manual (mirrors ship/SKILL.md step 8 screenshot rule and delegation-loop/SKILL.md's visible-change effort floor); prices from the 2026-10-08 fetch-models snapshot (models.dev)
frontend-ui.note: No numeric benchmark scores any model for UI work, so every entry here is a price judgment, not a measured result. No tier0: UI review escalates to tier2 on any user-visible change, so anything large or visible still runs on sonnet first. glm-5.3 leads tier1 at $1.40/$4.40 against sonnet at $2/$10; it has no UI score, so treat a small-UI dispatches to it as a cost saving of unproven quality, not a measured win.

translation.source: Alconost Translation Quality Index + Linguist Evaluation (2025-2026 sample, alconost.com/en/blog/best-llm-for-translation-2026); prices from the 2026-10-08 fetch-models snapshot (models.dev)
translation.note: No exact-model translation score exists for any model here. Alconost reports provider-family scores, not model-version scores, so those numbers are not assigned to any model row. deepseek-v4-pro leads tier1 for price ($0.66/$1.98) with no exact translation score; Claude stays the fallback inside tier1 and the top rung. No tier0: the old local: route had no score either and a text model on a local GPU is not the cheapest lane once paid prices are this low.

prose.source: LMArena Creative Writing leaderboard (BenchLeader snapshot, 2026-09-29) and EQ-Bench Creative Writing (Sept 2026) -- the two agree on a leader, unlike the translation sources; prices from the 2026-10-08 fetch-models snapshot (models.dev)
prose.note: EQ-Bench Creative Writing v3: fable 5.1 = 99.4% of the best score, opus 5 = 99.0%, gpt-6-astra = 99.2%. Every scored model here is expensive (opus $4/$20, fable $10/$50, astra $10/$50), so no cheap option is promoted on evidence: the scored rungs stay as they are, ordered by value (opus 6.6 pts/$ before fable 3.2 pts/$). sonnet has no creative-writing score and stays tier1, the cheapest Claude rung. No tier0: these leaderboards do not score a model currently routed for free, so tier0 quality is unknown.

cad-spatial.source: P3D-Bench (arxiv 2606.11152); prices from the 2026-10-08 fetch-models snapshot (models.dev)
cad-spatial.note: P3D-Bench geometry scores (opus 4.6 = 100%): kimi-k2.6 94.7%, deepseek-v4-pro 93.5%, mimo-v2.5-pro 91.2%, qwen3.6-plus 84.9%. Value (score percent / blended price): mimo-v2.5-pro 139.7 pts/$ at $0.435/$0.87, deepseek-v4-pro 70.8 at $0.66/$1.98, qwen3.6-plus 48.5 at $0.50/$3, kimi-k2.6 38.2 at $0.95/$4. The benchmark names Opus 4.6, DeepSeek V4 Pro and Qwen3.6-Plus, which are close to but not the same versions as the routed IDs, so treat the scores as a family signal rather than an exact match. tier1 is ordered by value and every entry scores at least 84.9% of the leader at a fraction of opus's $4/$20. opus keeps tier2 as the only 100% model. bmo stays tier0: the benchmark does not identify bmo's real served model, and tier0 means the lowest-cost routed option, not a model validated for CAD work.
